```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

# Import data
```{r}
# import TIRS_SISNAVE data for all possible cases 
suspected_cases <- 
  read.csv("data/TIRS_SINAVE_combined22_23_blockID.csv")

# import enrollment data: initial survey, informed consent and prospective survey
rn1 <- read.csv("data/RN1.csv")
rn2 <- read.csv("data/RN2.csv")
so1 <- read.csv("data/SO1.csv")

# import demographic data for SINAVE cases
moh <- read.csv("data/Sex_SINAVE.csv")

# import entomological and spraying coverage info
coverage <- read.csv("data/TIRS coverage.csv")
ento <- read.csv("data/TIRS_database_entom_summ.csv")

# import arms-blocks assignment (full list of all participating houses?)
arms <- read.csv("data/arms-blocks.csv")
```

# Data Exploration
## RN1
Cluster-level information, information on all households whether or not they joined the study
### Number of blocks?
```{r}
# initial consent form RN1
rn1 <- rn1 %>% 
  mutate(clrblk_id = str_sub(record_id, 1,4)) 

# number of unique blocks in the study
length(unique(rn1$clrblk_id))

# number of clusters just to double check
length(unique(rn1$cl_nr))
```
1529 blocks in the study, 54 unique cluster numbers...

### Number of people in a block?
```{r}
## number of all residential houses in a given block
num_res_houses <- rn1 %>% # id by block
  filter(rn1_rsdnt == 1) %>% # only residential houses
  group_by(clrblk_id) %>%
  summarize(count = n()) 
```
So we can find number of residential houses on a given block (see num_res_houses) but we only know the number of children within the household, nothing on adults.

### Number of children by block
```{r}
## all data, only residential houses
only_res <- subset(rn1, rn1_rsdnt == 1)

## check for missing data/see how many kids per house?
unique(only_res$rn1_kids_nr)
```
Some residences with 8 or 10 kids?
```{r}
# info on residences with more than three kids between 2-15
only_res %>%
  filter(rn1_kids_nr > 3) %>%
  arrange(rn1_kids_nr)

# distribution of kids per house
only_res %>%
  group_by(rn1_kids_nr) %>%
  summarize(count = n())
```
Does this look normal? Are there often many kids in one house?
Houses with 8 or more children are in blocks 3432, 5112, 5413, and 4322

Back to number of children per block
```{r}
# number of kids per block
kids_per_block <- only_res %>% 
  group_by(clrblk_id) %>%
  summarize(kids_per_block = sum(rn1_kids_nr))

# distribution of kids per block
kids_per_block %>%
  group_by(kids_per_block) %>%
  summarize(count = n())

# which ids?
kids_per_block %>% 
  filter(kids_per_block > 50)
```
Some blocks have 76 children?? Blocks 3316, 3317, and 3319 all have over 50 kids...all from the same cluster -- maybe a more residential area? These are different blocks (and a different cluster) from houses that indivudally have 8 or more children

## RN2
Second consent form, includes participant name, sex, date of birth...we can see which blocks participated in the study
### Number of participating clusters, blocks
```{r}
# id for unique block
rn2 <- rn2 %>% 
  mutate(clrblk_id = str_sub(record_id, 1,4),
         cl_nr = str_sub(record_id, 1,2))

# number of unique clusters
length(unique(rn2$cl_nr))

# number of unique block ids
length(unique(rn2$clrblk_id))
```
53 clusters now, 1307 blocks participating

### Reformat and get relevant information
record_id is now the same format as in the case dataset
```{r}
# change format of record id so it'll match what we have in the cases later
tirs_sex <- rn2 %>%
  filter(if_all(rn2_pt_id, complete.cases)) %>%
  select(record_id, rn2_pt_id, rn2_pt_sex) %>%
  rename(old_id = record_id) %>%
  mutate(record_id = paste0(old_id, LETTERS[rn2_pt_id]))
```


## SO1
Prospective survey, will know number of adults and children (male and female) in each participating house
### Number of participating clusters, blocks
```{r}
# id for unique block, info on household demographics
hh_demo <- so1 %>% 
  mutate(block_id = str_sub(record_id, 1,4),
         cl_nr = str_sub(record_id, 1,2)) %>%
  select(cl_nr, block_id, record_id, so1_male_nr, so1_male15_nr,
         so1_female_nr, so1_female15_nr)

# number of unique clusters
length(unique(hh_demo$cl_nr))

# number of unique block ids
length(unique(hh_demo$clrblk_id))
```
Still 53 clusters, 1157 blocks included in this survey

### Number of male and female adults, male and female children
```{r}
hh_demo <- hh_demo %>%
  mutate(male_adults = so1_male_nr - so1_male15_nr,
         female_adults = so1_female_nr - so1_female15_nr,
         total_adults = male_adults + female_adults,
         total_children = so1_male15_nr + so1_female15_nr,
         total_num_ppl = total_adults + total_children) 

# check to see if these make sense
## data entry errors?
so1 %>%
  filter(so1_male_nr < so1_male15_nr | so1_female_nr < so1_female15_nr)

## remove those three
so1_clean <- hh_demo %>%
  filter(so1_male_nr >= so1_male15_nr & so1_female_nr >= so1_female15_nr)

## households without any adults?
so1_clean %>%
  filter(total_adults <= 0)
```
data entry - three cases (212420, 213035, 606312) where there are more male/female children than total reported males/females in the house

25 houses with just teenagers/children?

```{r}
# reorganize dataset
so1_clean <- so1_clean %>%
  rename(total_males = so1_male_nr,
         total_females = so1_female_nr,
         male_children = so1_male15_nr,
         female_children = so1_female15_nr) %>%
  relocate(cl_nr, block_id, record_id, total_num_ppl,
           total_adults, total_children, male_adults, female_adults,
           male_children, female_children, total_males, total_females)
```


## MOH data
Sex of MOH cases, Year
### Recode variables to match with TIRS
Anything look weird? + recode to match with TIRS sex
```{r}
# no missing values, only male and female 
unique(moh$IDE_SEX)

# recode sex to match with what was used in TIRS -- 1, Female and 2, Male
# currently 1, Male and 2, Female
moh$sex <- ifelse(moh$IDE_SEX == 2, 1, 2)
```

## Case data
Suspected case data from TIRS and MOH surveillance
### Duplicates in the data?
```{r}
# check for duplicates in case data -- rows with same year and ID
scases <- suspected_cases
case_dupes <- suspected_cases %>%
  count(ID, Year) %>%
  filter(n > 1)
suspected_cases %>%
  semi_join(case_dupes, by = c("ID", "Year")) %>%
  arrange(Year, ID)
```
- All 7 SINAVE cases except for one have the exact same information in both lines -- just a duplicate? (same date of symptom onset and diagnosis). The other one has a different date of symptom onset and different diagnosis (goes from non-severe dengue to dengue with warning signs) -- but shouldn't this also be treated as the same case?
- As for the TIRS cases,
302432A has same symptom onset date, same diagnosis, but different commentary, and importantly, different lat/long coordinates which leads to a different block ID!!
401114A makes sense, participant got Zika and then Dengue a few months later

Just going to drop the exact duplicates for now:
```{r}
# check for exact duplicates
suspected_cases[duplicated(suspected_cases),]
# drop exact duplicates
# scases <- suspected_cases[!duplicated(suspected_cases),]
scases <- distinct(suspected_cases)
```

### Add deomographic data and organize dataset
```{r}
# join with MOH data
moh <- distinct(moh)
scases <- scases %>% 
  left_join(moh, by = join_by(ID == FOL_ID)) %>%
  select(!c(Year.y, IDE_SEX)) %>%
  left_join(tirs_sex, by = join_by(ID == record_id)) %>%
  mutate(Sex = ifelse(is.na(sex), rn2_pt_sex, sex)) %>%
  select(!c(sex, old_id, rn2_pt_id, rn2_pt_sex))

# reorganize dataset
cases <- scases %>%
  filter(Diagnosis != "Negativo") %>% # only case data?
  rename(Year = Year.x, 
         cluster_num = CLUSTER,
         block_num = MZTIRS,
         Block_Type = MZA3X3) %>%
  mutate(block_id = paste0(cluster_num, block_num)) %>%
  select(Year, Source, ID, Age, Sex, cluster_num, block_num, block_id, 
         Block_Type, TIRS, Onset_symp, Week_onset, Diagnosis, Comentario, 
         lon, lat, CVEGEO, CVE_MZA)
  
```

# Main Dataset
## Dataset with everyone in each participating house 
### All houses that did SO1
```{r}
# combine case data with all participating houses?
adults <- so1_clean %>%
  rename(house_id = record_id) %>%
  select(block_id, house_id, total_adults) %>%
  uncount(total_adults, .id = "adult_id") %>%
  mutate(adult_id = paste0(house_id, letters[adult_id]))

children <- so1_clean %>%
  rename(house_id = record_id) %>%
  select(block_id, house_id, total_children) %>%
  uncount(total_children, .id = "child_id") %>%
  mutate(child_id = paste0(house_id, LETTERS[child_id]))

full <- adults %>%
  bind_rows(children) %>%
  group_by(house_id) %>%
  mutate(id = ifelse(is.na(adult_id), child_id, adult_id)) %>%
  arrange(house_id) %>%
  select(!c(adult_id, child_id))
```

Merge with cases...
```{r}
# merge adults and children separately? since children have the same id but not adults
cases_children <- cases %>%
  filter(Source == "TIRS") %>%
  mutate(Case = 1)

# test full merge for children
test <- full %>%
  full_join(cases_children, by = join_by("id" == "ID", 
                                         "block_id" == "block_id")) %>%
  arrange(block_id)
```
Ok looking at this test full merge for children, maybe i should get more information in "full" first?

### All houses from RN1
```{r}
# by house
##  all houses and relevant information from rn1 // by record_id
rn1_full <- rn1 %>%
  select(record_id, rn1_br, rn1_rsdnt, rn1_kids_nr, rn1_cnst_n1, rn1_cnst_tirs) 

## join with so1 info // by record_id
so1_full <- so1 %>%
  select(record_id, so1_male_nr, so1_male15_nr,  so1_female_nr, so1_female15_nr)

rnso <- rn1_full %>%
  left_join(so1_full, by = "record_id")

# by person
## first extend dataset so each person is their own observation
full <- full %>%
  select(house_id, id) %>%
  rename(record_id = house_id)
  
per_person <- rnso %>%
  left_join(full, by = "record_id") %>%
  relocate(id, .before = record_id)

## join with info from rn2 // by person
rn2_full <- rn2 %>%
  mutate(id = ifelse(is.na(rn2_pt_id), NA, 
                     paste0(record_id, LETTERS[rn2_pt_id]))) %>%
  select(id, record_id, rn2_cnst_n2, rn2_pt_sex, rn2_kids_nr)

pp_rn2 <- per_person %>%
  left_join(rn2_full, by = join_by(id == id, record_id == record_id)) %>%
  relocate(id, .before = record_id)
  
## trial arm // by participant/person
arm <- arms %>%
  mutate(id = paste0(record_id, LETTERS[a_pt_id])) %>%
  select(id, record_id, a_arm, a_block)

pp_arm <- pp_rn2 %>%
  left_join(arm, by = join_by(id == id, record_id == record_id))

## cases // by person
### all kids cases...adult cases done by block?
trial_cases <- pp_arm %>%
  left_join(cases_children, by = join_by(id == ID)) %>%
  mutate(block_id = ifelse(is.na(block_id), 
                           str_sub(record_id, 1,4), block_id)) %>%
  relocate(block_id, .before = record_id)
```
So this is all the information I can add at an individual level...how can i add adult cases, and other block-level information?

Adding adult cases
```{r}
# all adult cases
cases_adults <- cases %>%
  filter(Source == "SINAVE") %>%
  mutate(Case = 1)

# one adult case is on block 1112 -- take a look at the people living there
trial_cases %>%
  filter(block_id == 1112)
```
A few non-residential buildings, 
So I'd want to look at (rn1_rsdnt == 1), (rn1_kids_nr != 0 [or NA]), 

Also...ID 113319D -- seems like they moved? Since the year is different!
```{r}
trial_cases %>%
  filter(record_id == 113319)
```

That said, are there any other instances where ID has been repeated?
```{r}
id_rep <- trial_cases %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarize(count = n()) %>%
  filter(count > 1)
id_rep <- id_rep[-13, ] # excluding NAs
```

Looking further into these individuals?
```{r}
trial_cases %>%
  filter(id %in% id_rep$id)
```
Ok most just got sick on different years, except 302432A and 401114A

Let's just look at those cases
```{r}
cases %>%
  filter(ID == "401114A" | ID == "302432A")
```
401114A makes sense, onset symptoms differ, as does diagnosis and week of onset...same block_id as well
302432A could be a duplicate? the everything is the same except commentary and lat/long....maybe i'll keep the coordinate with the same block_id as what is in the ID?
